block.title: init_cpu_features proved never to panic for any CPUID or XGETBV answer
block.p: Fil-C's user glibc asks the processor what it supports before it runs anything else. The function that does this is init_cpu_features. It gets its answers from three runtime calls, and it divides, shifts and indexes tables with them. The processor chooses the answers, so a proof has to cover all of them. This proof covers the function and every function it calls in the linked hi_atexit image.

The proof has one assumption about the processor, and the assumption is needed. get_common_cache_info walks the caches of CPUID leaf 4 and counts the subleaves in a signed 32-bit integer. A processor that never reported cache type zero up to subleaf 0x7fffffff would wrap the counter to a negative number, and the index into a table of sixteen rows computed from it would fail its bounds check. The world states the assumption as ow_leaf4_ends, and gcc_needs_leaf4 shows that the check fails without it.
No assumption about XSAVE is needed. The function calls zxgetbv only after it has seen the XSAVE bit in the answer for leaf 1, and the contract of zcpuid ties that bit to the kernel.

The linked image does not contain __tunables_init, so the tunable table holds the bytes of the image when the function runs. The function writes six rows. The rows that later startup code reads keep their type codes and their cleared initialized flags.

claim.p: Suppose that the processor's list of leaf 4 caches ends. Then a call of init_cpu_features runs without a panic, whatever the processor and the kernel answer. The initial globals of the image meet the precondition of the call.
